catalog_quote: p.68: "2.1 Words. Almost all recorded non-compound words are mono- or sesquisyllabic. Sesquisyllabic words consist of an unstressed minor syllable followed by a major syllable. There may be more polysyllabic words than can be inferred from the vocabulary given here, however. One reason for this is that I have not investigated the expressives, a wordclass that is rich in polysyllabic words in other Austroasiatic languages, such as Kammu ... 2.2 Major syllables. A major syllable consists of an onset consonant and a rhyme. ... Each major syllable has a tone (see 2.2.3). Whether minor syllables have tones or not has not been investigated." p.74: "2.2.3 Tones. U has a complicated tone system for an Austroasiatic language, with probably four contrasting tones. ... audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both deciding passages (p.68 secs 2.1/2.2; p.74 sec 2.2.3) are verbatim in the held page images of Svantesson 1988, and the PDF's pp.64-66 confirm the languoid is Pa Xep U = Glottolog uuuu1243. (2) Deciding source is a 1988 70-page phonology-centred grammar sketch by a phonetician with instrumental tone verification; Glottolog lists it as the only description of U, and Hsiu's 2017 Angkuic survey (fetched sources, open) confirms all Angkuic languages are tonal and that no fuller grammar/phonology of U exists. (3) Wishlist is two low-priority items (Svantesson 1989 Phonetica tonogenesis article, paywalled; Yan & Zhou 2012 Chinese survey, print) -- neither is expected to alter a TONAL / sesquisyllabic-iambic-by-word-shape coding.

sources.citation: Hsiu, Andrew. 2017. The Angkuic languages: a preliminary survey. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.1127808 (12 pp. + comparative spreadsheets).
sources.quote: p.1: 'All Angkuic languages are tonal (cf. Svantesson 1988, 1991).' ... 'U is documented by word lists of several hundred items. All others are very scantily documented. The only grammar of an Angkuic language is Chen's (2005) sketch grammar of Manmet.' No statement about stress; lists Svantesson 1988 as the source for U (Pa Xep).
sources.locator: p.1 'Background' bullets; pp.10-11 source list for Northern Angkuic (= U)
